title: Analysis and validation of programmed cell death genes associated with spinal cord injury progression based on bioinformatics and machine learning.
authors: Wang, Yongjie; Zhang, Zilin; Gong, Weiquan; Lv, Zhenshan; Qi, Jinwei; Han, Song; Liu, Boyuan; Song, Aijun; Yang, Zongyuan; Duan, Longfei; Zhang, Shaokun
one_liner_zh: 基于生物信息学和机器学习分析脊髓损伤中程序性细胞死亡基因，虽涉及转录因子预测但非蛋白质-DNA互作核心，无AI/物理模拟结合建模。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a severe condition affecting the central nervous system. It is marked by a high disability rate and potential for death. Research has demonstrated that programmed cell death (PCD) plays a significant role in the death of neuronal cells during SCI. The objective of our work was to illustrate the significant contribution of PCD genes in the progression of SCI. METHODS: SCI-related datasets GSE5296, GSE47681, and GSE189070 from the Gene Expression Omnibus database were comprehensively analyzed using bioinformatics methods. Common differentially expressed genes were validated by post-intersection screening with PCD genes. We constructed a gene prediction model using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator and the random forest algorithm to further screen for characteristic genes. We also performed Gene Ontology functional enrichment analysis and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes pathway analysis and generated a protein-protein interaction network, analyzed immune cell infiltration, and predicted upstream miRNAs and transcription factors. In animal experiments, we performed immunofluorescence staining of mouse SCI regions to verify gene expression. RESULTS: A total of five characteristic genes (Ctsd, Abca1, Cst7, Ctsb, and Cybb) were identified in our study and showed excellent diagnostic efficacy in predicting SCI progression (areas under the curve values of the five characteristic genes were 0.976 for Ctsd, 0.993 for Abca1, 0.995 of Cst7,0.986 of Ctsb, 0.959 of Cybb). These characterized genes were highly expressed at the site of SCI. Immune cell infiltration analysis revealed that multiple immune cells were involved in SCI progression. CONCLUSIONS: We identified five PCD genes (Ctsd, Abca1, Cst7, Ctsb, and Cybb) associated with SCI. This study helps to reveal the pathophysiologic influences of these genes on SCI and provides important insight for the development of more effective treatments.
abstract_zh: 背景：脊髓损伤（SCI）是一种影响中枢神经系统的严重疾病，其特点是高致残率和潜在致死风险。研究表明，程序性细胞死亡（PCD）在SCI期间神经元细胞死亡中发挥重要作用。我们工作的目的是阐明PCD基因在SCI进展中的显著贡献。方法：利用生物信息学方法，对来自基因表达综合数据库的SCI相关数据集GSE5296、GSE47681和GSE189070进行了全面分析。通过与PCD基因取交集筛选后，验证了常见的差异表达基因。我们使用最小绝对收缩和选择算子及随机森林算法构建了基因预测模型，以进一步筛选特征基因。我们还进行了基因本体功能富集分析和京都基因与基因组百科全书通路分析，生成了蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络，分析了免疫细胞浸润，并预测了上游miRNA和转录因子。在动物实验中，我们对小鼠SCI区域进行了免疫荧光染色以验证基因表达。结果：我们的研究共鉴定出五个特征基因（Ctsd、Abca1、Cst7、Ctsb和Cybb），它们在预测SCI进展方面表现出优异的诊断效能（五个特征基因的曲线下面积值分别为：Ctsd为0.976，Abca1为0.993，Cst7为0.995，Ctsb为0.986，Cybb为0.959）。这些特征基因在SCI部位高表达。免疫细胞浸润分析显示，多种免疫细胞参与SCI进展。结论：我们鉴定出五个与SCI相关的PCD基因（Ctsd、Abca1、Cst7、Ctsb和Cybb）。本研究有助于揭示这些基因对SCI的病理生理影响，并为开发更有效的治疗方法提供了重要见解。
